---
title: "An example chapter: logistic growth"
---

## The equation

A population $x(t)$ that grows at rate $r$ and saturates at the carrying
capacity $K$ obeys

$$
\frac{dx}{dt} = r\,x\left(1 - \frac{x}{K}\right),
$$ {#eq-logistic-ode}

whose solution for $x(0) = x_0$ is the logistic function{{< src logistic >}}

$$
x(t) = \frac{K}{1 + (K/x_0 - 1)\,e^{-rt}} .
$$ {#eq-logistic}

The core evaluates @eq-logistic directly; that it satisfies
@eq-logistic-ode is checked numerically to $10^{-7}$
{{< test logistic_solves_the_ode "ODE residual" >}}, and the limits
$x(0) = x_0$ and $x(\infty) = K$ are checked as well
{{< test logistic_limits "limits" >}}. The construction goes back to
@verhulst1838.

Two conventions of the format are visible in the paragraph above. The
superscript ⟨logistic⟩ links to the API documentation of the function that
evaluates the equation, and the ✓ badges link to the tests. Neither
interrupts the reading, and `make check` fails the build if either target
disappears.

Drag the growth rate and the carrying capacity. The plot zooms with the
wheel, pans by dragging, resets on a double click, and the toolbar switches
the axes between linear and logarithmic scaling and downloads the curve as
SVG or CSV. The same experiment opens in the laboratory, where every
